newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish inflation to end '97 below 2 pct -Rojo.
newsitem.headline: Spanish inflation to end '97 below 2 pct -Rojo.

text.p: Spanish central bank governor Luis Angel Rojo said on Wednesday that inflation is likely to end 1997 below 2.0 percent after a slight summer pick-up.

"The forecasts allow one to think that inflation could stabilise, even show a slight pick-up in the summer, but remain below two percent in the remaining part of the year," Rojo said in a parliamentary speech.
He added that monetary policy would remain prudent.

Rojo said monetary policy would remain as prudent as it had been so far, eyeing any potential market volatility on changing expectations over Spain's possibility to enter European Economic and Monetary union (EMU).

"The fact markets are focused on the expectations of (Spanish) entrance into EMU means volatility and risk of price fluctuation which is, I fear, inevitable until the final choice of countries," he said.

"Economic policies need to have a certain scope of manoeuvre to face possible future fluctuations in financial markets. This is the reason why the Bank of Spain is using prudently the scope for possible reductions in its money market rate."
Spain's April CPI fell to a record low at 1.7 percent rise year-on-year versus 2.2 percent in March.
The central bank governor said the contention of inflation was due not only to monetary policy, but also to fiscal consolidation and to the government's liberalisation measures.
He highlighted the fact that Spain does not yet meet the Maastricht criteria for inflation, which refers to the average of the last 12 months.
"But (Spanish inflation) will meet also that requirement in the coming months," he said.
